contentSummary: Lines are instrumental in coming up with different design on paper or on electronic garget. Different lines carry different meaning in profile design. Through lines technocrats are able to interpret data and commutate effectively. This topic will focus on drawing of different lines.

Drawing different types of lines using instrumentsTask: Drawing lines Learners to draw different types of lines using instruments TIPS: −Demonstrate proper use of drawing instruments• Start with tracing tasks to help learners understand movement and alignment. • Show learners how to place the ruler flat on the paper and hold it steady with one hand.• Slowly draw a line with one hand, narrating the steps (Hold the ruler with one hand... draw along the edge) • Give hands on practice, let learner practice with real rulers in pairs or small groups.• Remind learners that neatness matters than spee

exercises: CRITERIA: Assess Learners’ ability to: - recognize and name different types of lines.- associate line types with their correct names- draw different types of lines freely and creatively.- use instruments correctly to draw precise lines. Assess accuracy and variety in lines drawn on the board (do they include straight, zigzag, wavy?). SUMMARY Lines play an important role in creating and understanding designs, whether on paper or electronic devices. Each type of line has its own meaning and can be used to express different ideas in profile designs. By learning how to draw and identify different lines, learners develop the ability to communicate visually and interpret design data effectively.

contentSummary: Paper is can be used to make many useful and decorative items. This topic will help learners explore different paper craft techniques by creating items such as chains, belts, masks, and simple models. Collage, an art technique where pictures are created by sticking different materials like paper, cloth, or leaves onto a surface. Using a variety of papers, learners will design own unique collage pictures. This will help learners’ express creativity while improving cutting, folding, and design skills.
learnerActivities: ACTIVITY 1: Identifying Items Made in Paper CraftTask: Name and describe each item Learners name and describe examples of paper craft items. TIP: −Briefly explain that paper craft involves creating decorative or functional items using different types of paper and folding, cutting, gluing, or molding techniques −Show learners various paper craft items. These can include: Greeting cards, Origami figures, Paper flowers, Paper baskets, Paper beads, Wall decorations, Paper fans, Envelopes, Gift boxes.Ask learners to:- Name each item.- Discuss what the item could be used for.- Identify the type of

Making Various Items Using PaperTask: Making Items Using Paper Learners choose one or more items to make such as (Greeting card, Paper flower, Paper fan, Paper chain, Simple origami (boat, hat, bird), Paper bead bracelet or necklace...) Learners display their items on a table, mat or classroom wall and describe the items made. TIP: −Recap

briefly (what paper craft is and examples of items). −Show simple examples of paper crafts (a greeting card, a flower, a paper fan, or a small gift box...). −Demonstrate step-by-step how to make the item(s). −Use clear instructions and model each step (cutting, folding, gluing, decorating)Demonstration −Guide Learners as they:• Select their paper and materials• Follow steps to make their items• Decorate or personalize their items −Let learners display their items on a table, mat or classroom wall. −Invite each learner or group to briefly explain what they made.

Make different pictures using collage technique Learners cut out shapes from old magazines, coloured paper, or newspapers. Learners Glue the pieces onto a larger sheet to form a picture. Learners add details by layering and arranging pieces creatively.
assessmentCriteria: Different pictures using collage technique made appropriately.
exercises: CRITERIA: Assess ability to identify paper craft items from pictures. Assess ability to make at least one item using paper. Assess the practice of making their own paper items.

CRITERIA Assess learners’ ability to:- use different materials and arrange them creatively.- demonstrate originality and personal style in their artwork.- express ideas visually through collage.- Demonstrate the use of colour, texture, shape, and composition creatively.

contentSummary: Modeling is a fun, hands-on way for learners to create objects using clay or plasticine. By shaping animals, dolls, fruits, and birds, learners strengthen their creativity, finger strength, and imagina-tion.
learnerActivities: Free-form Clay ModelingTask: Object Creation Learners to model free form objects (animals, birds, fruits, dolls...)TIP: −Show pictures or real examples of objects to be modeled. −Demonstrate rolling, flattening, and shaping clay/ plasticine into basic forms. −Let learners choose what to make, encouraging their own ideas. −Provide help as needed and allow peer sharing. −Arrange completed models for a class display or gallery.
assessmentCriteria: Objects modelled using clay/ plasticine accordingly.
exercises: CRITERIA: Assess ability to: - Mold clay into identifiable objects with basic form and balance.- Demonstrate creativity and safe handling of tools and materials.SUMMARYIn this topic, learners explore crafts through paper and modeling activities. They create decorative items, collage pictures, and molded figures using hands-on methods. These activities help learners develop creativity, coordination, and appreciation of handmade work. Through playful learning, they also build problem-solving and communication skills while having fun.

contentSummary: Designing letters of the alphabet allows learners to explore creative ways of making and decorating letter forms. By engaging in hands-on activities like copying, cutting out, and painting, learners enhance their understanding of the alphabet while expressing themselves artistically. These activities help in developing both literacy and motor coordination skills.
learnerActivities: Designing letters of the alphabet (copy, cut out, paint letters ...)Task 1: Guided Letter Copying• Learners recognize and reproduce letters by copying.TIP: −Display an alphabet chart and point to each letter while naming it. −Write a few selected letters on the board and model how to copy them. −Provide learners with dotted-line letter worksheets for tracing. (optional) −Move around the classroom offering individual support as learners copy letters into their exercise books.Task 2: Letter Decoration Challenge −Learners to design letters by decorating them creatively.TIP:- Distribute printed ou
teachingMaterials: Alphabet charts or flashcards White paper or drawing books Crayons
glue sticks Pre-cut letter stencils or templates Cardboard or colored construction paper Paints
assessmentCriteria: Letters of the alphabet designed accordingly
exercises: CRITERIA: Assess learners’ ability to: - Recognize and name the letter- Copied letters, clearly shaped and proportional- Use creative decoration techniques- Cut and paste lettersSUMMARY In this topic, learners are introduced to lettering - the creative art of designing and decorating letters of the alphabet. Through engaging, hands-on activities such as copying, decorating, cutting, and painting, learners explore various ways of forming letters using different materials and tools. These practical experiences help learners develop fine motor skills, enhance their creativity, improve letter recognition, and strengthen early writing abilities.

Go to the toilet, wash your hands, Then you’re ready to splash and stand!” −Add simple movements to the rhyme for fun and memory.
teachingMaterials: flip-flops) Music or rhymes about pool rules
assessmentCriteria: Rules on pool hygiene demonstrated correctly.
exercises: CRITERIA: Assess learners’ ability to:- name and demonstrate pool hygiene steps- recognise good hygiene habits- participate in role-play and discussion- expression verbal hygiene rules through songs or chants.SUMMARYIn this topic, learners are introduced to the importance of pool hygiene as part of swimming activities. Through visual aids, role-play, and fun games, they learn how to shower before swimming, use the toilet, and avoid unhygienic practices. These simple but vital actions help keep the swimming environment clean and healthy, while also fostering responsibility, awareness, and social skills.
